observation_summary: The RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS feature was incorrectly forcing all deep-stubbed mocks to be serializable, regardless of whether the parent mock was configured to be serializable. This caused exceptions when the return type did not meet the requirements for serialization.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved changing the logic for how serialization settings are propagated from the parent mock to the deep-stubbed mock. Instead of unconditionally calling .serializable(), the code now uses a new method 'propagateSerializationSettings' to check the parent's serialization mode. This is a correction of the procedural logic used to configure the mock, fitting the Algorithm/Method category.
evidence_used: The fix modifies the 'withSettingsUsing' method to call 'propagateSerializationSettings' instead of unconditionally calling 'mockSettings.serializable()'.
The new 'propagateSerializationSettings' method correctly retrieves the serialization mode from the parent mock settings.
The 'newDeepStubMock' method signature was updated to accept the parent mock, allowing the propagation of its settings.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves setting a value (serialization mode), the core issue is the logic of how that value is derived and propagated through the mock creation process, which is a procedural/algorithmic concern.
The fix changes internal method signatures and logic within the same component (ReturnsDeepStubs), rather than fixing a contract mismatch between two distinct modules.
